text:
jia: Observed a regression on prod after the kernel-selector change. Latency P95 up ~12% and GPU mem pressure spikes. Looks correlated with KV cache hit-rate drop for prompt prefixes. logs + profile attached inline.

sam: Thanks. Do you have a perf profile and cache metrics (hitrate by prefix length/cohort)?

jia: Quick dump:
```
[2026-03-17T22:41:02Z] model=a1 seq=512 batch=8 kernel=fast-attn mem_used_gpu=14.2GB kv_hits=0.62 kv_misses=0.38 evicts/sec=3.4 OOM=false
[2026-03-17T22:41:18Z] model=a1 seq=512 batch=16 kernel=fast-attn mem_used_gpu=15.6GB kv_hits=0.49 kv_misses=0.51 evicts/sec=12.1 OOM=true
```
notice the hit-rate collapse when batching increases + kernel switch.

maria: Two hypotheses: 1) kernel path increases per-request KV footprint (different slot alignment) so key normalization mismatch; 2) eviction/TTL buckets are too coarse so warm prefixes get evicted when batch sizes oscillate.

lee: Also saw fragmentation in GPU allocator after repeated evictions, free lists not coalescing -> higher peak usage. Could be slab fragmentation from variable sized KV entries.

nina: Can we reproduce in staging with synthetic traffic? I can spin up a workload that toggles batch sizes and kernel selection.

jia: Yes please. Repro script idea: ramp batch 8 -> 16 -> 32, maintain same prompt prefixes with jittered suffixes. Collect: kernel path, kv_key_hash, kv_slot_size, ttl_bucket, allocator free map.

sam: For immediate mitigation, suggested config patch: lower TTL buckets on GPU cache for small prefixes and enable compact-on-evict. Config snippet: 
```
cache:
  gpu:
    ttl_buckets: [1s,5s,15s,60s,300s]
    compact_on_evict: true
    max_slots: 1_200_000
    lru_bias: 0.6  # age-weighted preference
```
Apply to canary and monitor.

maria: I worry compact_on_evict = true might add CPU overhead. Maybe use probabilistic compaction: 5% chance per eviction to run compaction.

lee: Another approach: normalize keys at ingress so kernel-specific padding/kv-slot differences don't change key identity. Add canonicalizer: strip model-padding token and trailing zeros.

jia: Agreed. Proposal: 1) canonicalize keys in runtime ingress; 2) add mini-compaction sweep (probabilistic) on evict spikes; 3) temporarily cap batch size per-slot for hot prefixes to avoid transient misses.

nina: I'll run the staging experiment and post results. ETA ~2h.

ops-bot: @channel Deploy started: cluster=staging region=us-west-2 config=ttl-prob-compaction-canary user=nina

sam: Also flagging for kernel team: if kernel alters memory layout of KV entries we need a deterministic slot serializer across kernels. cc @eng-runtime-kernel.

jia: Thanks everyone. Let's reconvene after the staging run. If staging reproduces, we'll roll to prod canary with conservative TTL bucket changes and key canonicalization. :thumbsup:
